contexts.text: Those who are called drunkards from wine or strong drink. Explained, Illustrated. AC 3069.
Strong drink, etc. are predicated of the things of the understanding.
Strong drink, by which they err () = truths mixed with falsities.

That they will be averse to all things which agree with truths, is signified by strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it (). Strong drink = the things which are from truths and which agree with them. ( = the truth of good made undelightful by its falsification and adulteration). AE 618:4.
These err through wine, and through strong drink they are gone astray () = through falsities and through such things as are from falsities...
Wine, in special, = the truth of the spiritual and thence of the rational man; and strong drink () = the derivative truth of the natural man.
As such love falsities and things falsified, it is added, Come, I will take wine, and we will be drunken with strong drink ().
To follow strong drink () = to hatch doctrinals from themselves.
To mingle strong drink () = to confirm falsities.
Heroes to drink wine = those who adulterate the truth of the Word; men of strength to mingle strong drink () = those who falsify it.
In Heaven there appear... strong drinks, etc.
